newsitem.title: USA: CONSOLIDATED ECO SETTLES WITH DEBENTURE HOLDER.
newsitem.headline: CONSOLIDATED ECO SETTLES WITH DEBENTURE HOLDER.

text.p: Consolidated Eco-Systems Inc said Friday it has agreed to settle with Shaar Fund Ltd issues involving conversion into stock of $1.25 million debentures that the fund bought from Consolidated in December.
Under a settlement agreement, Consolidated said it would issue 2.2 million shares for part of the debentures that the fund had sought to convert.

In addition, the fund will be able to convert the remainder of the debentures for about 1.3 million additional shares at a conversion rate of $0.45 per share, said Sam Sexton, general counsel and executive vice president of Consolidated.
"They wanted to convert when our stock price was as low as $0.06, and they sought more than 5.8 million shares, which we did not honor," Sexton said.
He added that, of the initial 2.2 million shares agreed to, the fund had already sold 2.0 million shares and only 200,000 shares may be sold in the future.

Consolidated said that under the agreement, the fund would reimburse it $100,000 in previously incurred expenses and shoulder up to $50,000 to cover future legal fees in resolving questions related to the debentures' conversion.

Consolidated provides site remediation solutions, coal and petroleum tar liquefication and recycling, hazardous waste/spill cleanup services, civil and environmental engineering and other related services.
